These Dancing With The Stars Season 35 Pros Have Never Won A Mirrorball

By  Lorianne Palinkas

Try something different:

Dancing With The Stars season 35 features 16 professional dancers and their celebrity dance partners, and half of them have never won the show's coveted Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy. Hosted by Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough and judged by Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli, and Derek Hough, Dancing With The Stars season 35 premieres with a two-night event on Tuesday, September 15 and Wednesday, September 16 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC.

The Dancing With The Stars season 35 celebrity contestants and their professional dance partners include Olympic figure skater Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov, Summer House star Ciara Miller and Brandon Armstrong, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Conner Leavitt and Adele Zaikman, stand-up comedian and podcaster Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold, Paralympic track and field athlete Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach, celebrity chef and entrepreneur Giada DeLaurentiis and Alan Bersten, Jimmy Kimmel Live! star Guillermo Rodriguez and Witney Carson, and actor and dancer Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson.

The Dancing With The Stars season 35 cast also features Savannah Bananas second baseman Jackson Olson and Emma Slater, actress and dancer Jenna Dewan and Val Chmerkovskiy, actress and director Julia Stiles and Ezra Sosa, television personality and model Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas, Love Thy Nader star Sarah Jane Nader and Hailey Bills, actress and singer Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik, Hanson frontman Taylor Hanson and Britt Stewart, and The Bachelorette star Tyler Cameron and Sharna Burgess.

Out of the 16 professional dancers competing in Dancing With The Stars season 35, half of them are previous winners. They include three-time winners Mark (season 6 with Kristi Yamaguchi, season 8 with Shawn Johnson, and season 31 with Charli D'Amelio) and Val (season 20 with Rumer Willis, season 23 with Laurie Hernandez, and season 32 with Xochitl Gomez); two-time winners Witney (season 19 with Alfonso Ribeiro and season 34 with Robert Irwin) and Jenna (season 26 with Adam Rippon and season 33 with Joey Graziadei); and one-time winners Emma (season 24 with Rashad Jennings); Sharna (season 27 with Bobby Bones); Alan (season 28 with Hannah Brown); and Daniella (season 30 with Iman Shumpert). Here are the eight Dancing With The Stars season 35 professional dancers who've never won, but are hoping to take home their first Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy this year.

Brandon Armstrong

Dancing With The Stars season 35 marks Brandon's ninth season with the show after he made his debut in season 27 with Tinashe. Although he's never won, the closest he came was in season 33 when he placed 3rd with Chandler Kinney. Brandon has also competed with Mary Wilson (season 28, placed 12th); Jeannie Mai (season 29, placed 9th); Kenya Moore (season 30, placed 10th); Jordin Sparks (season 31, placed 9th); Lele Pons (season 32, placed 8th); and Lauren Jauregui (season 34, placed 11th). It'll be exciting to see if Brandon can move from the middle of the pack to the top of the leaderboard with his season 35 partner, Ciara Miller.

Pasha Pashkov

Pasha made his Dancing With The Stars debut as a professional dancer in season 28, and season 35 is his eighth season with the show. The closest he came to winning was in season 32 when he placed 3rd with Ariana Madix. Other than Ariana, Pasha and his celebrity partners have consistently been eliminated early in the competition. They've included Kate Flannery (season 28, placed 7th); Carole Baskin (season 29, placed 14th); Christine Chiu (season 30, placed 14th); Teresa Giudice (season 31, placed 15th); Tori Spelling (season 33, placed 12th); and Danielle Fishel (season 34, placed 8th). With Olympic figure skater Amber Glenn as his partner for season 35, perhaps Pasha will have a better chance of going further in the competition.

Britt Stewart

Britt became a professional dancer on Dancing With The Stars in season 29, and season 35 is her seventh season. The farthest she ever went in the competition was in season 31 when she placed 5th with her celebrity dance partner and eventual husband, Daniel Durant. In season 29, her debut, she placed 6th with Johnny Weir. However, in every other season, Britt has been eliminated quite early with her celebrity partners, including Martin Kove (season 30, placed 15th); Adrian Peterson (season 32, placed 11th); Eric Roberts (season 33, placed 10th); and Baron Davis (season 34, placed 13th/14th). It'll be intriguing to see how far Britt goes in Dancing With The Stars season 35 with her celebrity dance partner, Taylor Hanson.

Rylee Arnold

Dancing With The Stars season 35 is Rylee's fourth season with the show. The highest she's ever placed was 4th with Stephen Nedoroscik in season 33. Rylee has also danced with Harry Jowsey (season 32, placed 6th) and Scott Hoying (season 34, placed 10th). Perhaps Rylee can make it to the finals again in season 35 with her celebrity dance partner, Connor Wood, and maybe even win.

Ezra Sosa

Ezra has been a Dancing With The Stars pro for two seasons. He made his debut as a pro in season 33 when he was paired with Anna Delvey, and they placed 13th. Anna was one of the most controversial contestants in the history of the show, as she danced with a bedazzled ankle bracelet due to her past legal issues. In Dancing With The Stars season 34, Ezra placed 3rd with Jordan Chiles, making it all the way to the finale. With Julia Stiles as his partner in season 35, Ezra is almost certain to go far in the competition again.

Jan Ravnik

Dancing With The Stars season 35 is Jan's second as a pro on the show, after he placed 9th with Jen Affleck in season 34. Jan joined Dancing With The Stars after performing as one of Taylor Swift's backup dancers during her Eras tour. It's going to be exciting to see what Jan does in his second year with the show, and how far he can take his celebrity dance partner, Tatyana Ali.

Hailey Bills

Hailey is making her debut as a Dancing With The Stars pro in season 35, after performing as a member of the troupe in season 34, so this is her first time competing on the show. She previously competed in Dancing With The Stars: Juniors, along with her partner Tripp Johnston, and they placed 11th/12th. Their mentor was Jenna Johnson, who's Hailey's aunt. It's going to be fun to see Hailey move from the troupe to center stage as a pro on Dancing With The Stars season 35 with her celebrity dance partner, Sarah Jane Nader.

Adele Zaikman

Adele joins Dancing With The Stars season 35 after winning Dancing With The Stars: The Next Pro, so this is her first time competing on the main show. Throughout the spinoff series, she received rave reviews from the judges, Shirley Ballas, Mark Ballas, and a group of rotating guest judges. She was praised for her extraordinary talent, teaching ability, and professionalism. It's going to be thrilling to see Adele bring her expertise to Dancing With The Stars and perhaps win both shows in one year.

Dancing With The Stars season 35 premieres with a two-night event on Tuesday, September 15 and Wednesday, September 16 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC.

Dancing with the Stars is a popular dancing competition reality TV show airing on ABC and Disney+. The series features various celebrities who pair with professional dancers to compete in front of a panel of judges. The US version of the UK TV show Strictly Come Dancing premiered in 2005 and was originally hosted by Tom Bergeron for its first 28 seasons.
